text: Meet the compliance manager of an export garment factory in Bangladesh, thirty days before a buyer audit. The fire safety certificate expires before the auditor arrives, and nobody has noticed yet.

Apparel and home textiles are 83 percent of Bangladesh's exports, and the E U buys about half of its garments. Buyers demand proof, and E U due-diligence rules raise the bar. Yet the proof lives in scattered P D Fs, and gaps surface during the audit.

ThreadLight is an AI compliance copilot. It reads the factory's documents, links every buyer requirement to its evidence in a graph, flags gaps and contradictions with a cited source, plans the fixes, and writes the report in English and Bangla. The difference: rules, not the model, decide dates and status, and only a named person can close a finding. Everything in this demo uses synthetic data.
Six documents come in. Here, extraction is a pre-computed sample; the rule stages run live.
One fire certificate supports two requirements. If it lapses, both fail.
Every finding cites its source. Integrity alerts catch a certificate number that is not on file, and a fix marked complete with no proof.
Renew the certificate, and coverage jumps from 29 to 55 percent.
We assign it and upload the renewal. It is pending human review, so coverage stays at 29. The system cannot close it. A named compliance officer approves, and only then can it close.
The report separates verified from open, in English or Bangla.

Under the hood: input is certificates, scans and buyer codes, in English or Bangla. O C R and a language model extract fields as structured data with page citations. Retrieval-augmented matching links each clause to candidate evidence, and a knowledge graph ties them together. Deterministic rules decide the status, and a model drafts bilingual explanations for a person to approve. Today the graph, rules and report run live; extraction and retrieval are next.

The value is fewer audit surprises and faster, provable fixes. In a pilot we will measure evidence-preparation hours, the share of requirements with cited, in-date evidence, issues found before the audit, and time to an approved closure. Next: pilot with export factories, real O C R and retrieval, and Bangla document reading. ThreadLight: evidence you can verify, before the auditor asks.
